headline: Benchmarks show perturbation rankings and responses often fail to generalize across datasets, cohorts and cell lines
label: Reliability Audits For Biological Design
summary: New benchmarks test whether drug and CRISPRi perturbation responses and computational corrections hold across sources, cohorts, and cell lines.
synthesis: The dominant thread is auditing whether perturbation-derived results and computational methods remain valid beyond their derivation setting. One preprint reports limited cross-source concordance among six drug-perturbation transcriptomic resources. TRACE finds CRISPRi rejuvenation rankings shift with aging cohort and track proliferation programs. A Perturb-seq study finds knockdown transfer to new cell lines requires screening part of each line, motivating CASTER. Method papers pair new tools with explicit comparison: anchor-guided batch correction is benchmarked against ComBat on TCGA, ARC-Impute across 17 spatial datasets, and DeepRNAi releases a training and benchmark set for siRNA activity. The shared emphasis is on concordance testing and benchmark release rather than in-distribution performance. Other items, such as the kinetic-model and CellStressDB reports, are resource or mechanistic contributions and only loosely connected.
